summary: @onereach/orest-vue-demi-vue3 preinstall side-loads Bun to execute an obfuscated bundled payload
details: The package advertises itself as a Vue3 vue-demi re-export shim (dist/index.mjs contains only globalThis['VueDemi'] re-exports), but its package.json declares a preinstall hook `node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs checks whether `bun` is on PATH, and if not, downloads the Bun v1.3.13 runtime archive from GitHub, extracts the binary to a temporary directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it via execFileSync against a bundled sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a ~727KB obfuscator.io-style bundle (rotated string-array `n7gIxM`, rotation function `WV8StW`, hex-suffixed identifiers, `// @bun @bun-cjs` header) whose contents and purpose are not documented anywhere in the package and bear no relation to a Vue3 shim. Executing the payload under a freshly downloaded alternate runtime means Node-based supply-chain and dependency-scanning tooling that hooks Node lifecycle scripts never observes the code that actually runs. The advertised library surface is a decoy; the executed code is opaque and runs on every `npm install`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
